# tar interop golden fixtures — generated by GNU tar 1.35, committed hermetic.

Regenerate deterministically (needs a SEEK_HOLE-capable fs, e.g. tmpfs):

```bash
D=/tmp/fixgen; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D/in && cd $D/in
python3 -c "
f=open('sparse2.bin','wb')
f.write(b'HEAD'); f.seek(4*1024*1024); f.write(b'MID')
f.truncate(8*1024*1024); f.close()
f=open('sparse8.bin','wb')
for i in range(8):
    f.seek(i*1024*1024); f.write(bytes([65+i])*100)
f.truncate(8*1024*1024); f.close()"
mkdir -p long && cd long
printf 'plain content' > hello.txt
mkdir -p sub && printf 'nested content' > sub/deep.txt
python3 -c "import os; os.makedirs('a'*60, exist_ok=True)"
python3 -c "open('a'*60 + '/' + 'b'*80 + '.txt','w').write('split-name payload')"
ln -s hello.txt alink
python3 -c "open('c'*150,'w').write('pax-fallback payload')"
printf 'utf8 payload' > 'héllo-世界.txt'
printf 'future payload' > future.txt && touch -d '2500-01-01 UTC' future.txt
touch -d '2020-01-01 UTC' hello.txt sub/deep.txt \
  "$(python3 -c "print('a'*60)")/bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb.txt" \
  "$(python3 -c "print('c'*150)")" 'héllo-世界.txt'
touch -h -d '2020-01-01 UTC' alink
touch -d '2020-01-01 UTC' ../sparse2.bin ../sparse8.bin ../long/sub
cd $D
tar --format=gnu --sparse --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner \
  -cf sparse-gnu.tar -C in sparse2.bin
tar --format=gnu --sparse --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner \
  -cf sparse-gnu-ext.tar -C in sparse8.bin
tar --format=pax --sparse --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner \
  --pax-option=delete=atime,delete=ctime \
  -cf sparse-pax10.tar -C in sparse2.bin
tar --format=ustar --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner \
  -cf ustar-long.tar -C in/long hello.txt sub alink \
  "$(python3 -c "print('a'*60)")/bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb.txt"
tar --format=pax --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner \
  --pax-option=delete=atime,delete=ctime \
  -cf pax-long.tar -C in/long hello.txt sub alink \
  "$(python3 -c "print('c'*150)")" 'héllo-世界.txt' future.txt
```

Facts pinned by these fixtures:

- GNU ustar refuses slashless >100 names and far-future mtime
  (`--owner=3000000`, year 2500 both rejected) — our writer is a superset there.
- `sparse-gnu.tar` / `sparse-gnu-ext.tar`: oldgnu `S` typeflag, map at
  header offset 386, realsize at 483, extension-chain flag at 482/504.
- `sparse-pax10.tar`: pax 1.0, map prepended to stored data as decimal
  text (`count, offset, size, ...` + `(realsize, 0)` terminator), data entry
  named `./GNUSparseFile.PID/name`.
- `pax-long.tar` `future.txt`: mtime 16725225600 exceeds 12-char octal,
  carried only by the pax record (ustar field zero).
